title: When Suffering Becomes Medicine
subtitle: Raag Aasaa
summary: Guru Nanak does not glorify pain. He exposes how comfort can sedate remembrance while suffering can reopen dependence on the Creator.
whyItMatters: This shabad reframes hard seasons without trivializing them and helps a user move from resentment toward reverent honesty.
takeaway: Hardship is not automatically holy, but it can become the place where reality is finally faced.

lines.gurmukhi: ਦੁਖੁ ਦਾਰੂ ਸੁਖੁ ਰੋਗੁ ਭਇਆ ਜਾ ਸੁਖੁ ਤਾਮਿ ਨ ਹੋਈ ॥
lines.transliteration: dhukh dhaaroo sukh rog bhiaa jaa sukh taam na hoiee ||
lines.translation: Suffering is the medicine, and pleasure the disease, because where there is pleasure, there is no desire for God.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੂੰ ਕਰਤਾ ਕਰਣਾ ਮੈ ਨਾਹੀ ਜਾ ਹਉ ਕਰੀ ਨ ਹੋਈ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: too(n) karataa karanaa mai naahee jaa hau karee na hoiee ||1||
lines.translation: You are the Creator Lord; I can do nothing. Even if I try, nothing happens. ||1||
I am a sacrifice to Your almighty creative power which is pervading everywhere.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੇਰਾ ਅੰਤੁ ਨ ਜਾਈ ਲਖਿਆ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: teraa a(n)t na jaiee lakhiaa ||1|| rahaau ||

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਾਤਿ ਮਹਿ ਜੋਤਿ ਜੋਤਿ ਮਹਿ ਜਾਤਾ ਅਕਲ ਕਲਾ ਭਰਪੂਰਿ ਰਹਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: jaat meh jot jot meh jaataa akal kalaa bharapoor rahiaa ||
lines.translation: Your Light is in Your creatures, and Your creatures are in Your Light; Your almighty power is pervading everywhere.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਸਿਫਤਿ ਸੁਆਲਿੑਉ ਜਿਨਿ ਕੀਤੀ ਸੋ ਪਾਰਿ ਪਇਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: too(n) sachaa saahib sifat suaali(h)au jin keetee so paar piaa ||
lines.translation: You are the True Lord and Master; Your Praise is so beautiful. One who sings it, is carried across.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਕਰਤੇ ਕੀਆ ਬਾਤਾ ਜੋ ਕਿਛੁ ਕਰਣਾ ਸੁ ਕਰਿ ਰਹਿਆ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: kahu naanak karate keeaa baataa jo kichh karanaa su kar rahiaa ||2||
lines.translation: Nanak speaks the stories of the Creator Lord; whatever He is to do, He does. ||2||

structure: Begins with the startling inversion of pain and pleasure.
Moves quickly into dependence on the Creator, not self-management.
Ends in awe at the Creator's all-pervading presence and action.

evidence.coreClaim: Guru Nanak does not glorify pain. He exposes how comfort can sedate remembrance while suffering can reopen dependence on the Creator.
